elements.quote: The second iteration of this living NMA includes 32 randomised trials which enrolled 25 147 participants and addressed 21 different prophylactic drugs; adding 21 trials (66%), 18 162 participants (75%) and 16 (76%) prophylactic drugs.
elements.reason: This provides the total number of included studies/trials and participants, and summarizes relevant review characteristics (number of prophylactic drugs addressed).

elements.quote: Of the 16 prophylactic drugs analysed, none provided convincing evidence of a reduction in the risk of laboratory confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. For admission to hospital and mortality outcomes, no prophylactic drug proved different than standard care or placebo. Hydroxychloroquine and vitamin C combined with zinc probably increase the risk of adverse effects leading to drug discontinuation-risk difference for hydroxychloroquine (RD) 6 more per 1000 (95% credible interval (CrI) 2 more to 10 more); for vitamin Ccombinedwith zinc, RD 69 more per 1000 (47 more to 90 more), moderate certainty evidence.
elements.reason: Main outcomes are reported with direction and effect summaries (e.g., infection, hospital admission, mortality, adverse effects). However, the evidence does not indicate the number of included studies and participants for each outcome in a structured way.

Although credible intervals are mentioned for some effects, the abstract reporting of the summary estimate and its confidence/credible interval for a meta-analysis is not clearly provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Hydroxychloroquine and vitamin C combined with zinc probably increase the risk of adverse effects leading to drug discontinuation-risk difference for hydroxychloroquine (RD) 6 more per 1000 (95% credible interval (CrI) 2 more to 10 more); for vitamin Ccombinedwith zinc, RD 69 more per 1000 (47 more to 90 more), moderate certainty evidence.
elements.reason: When groups are compared, the direction of effect is stated (increased adverse effects), but it is not clearly described in terms of which group is favored for each main comparison/outcome.

elements.quote: This review was not registered. The protocol established a priori is included as a supplement.
elements.reason: It is stated that the review was not registered, but no register name and registration number are provided.
The retrieved evidence does not describe the current state of knowledge and important uncertainties in the context of the review rationale.
The retrieved evidence does not explicitly explain the importance and need for conducting the review as part of the Introduction rationale.

Although the retrieved evidence mentions that this is the second version and replaces a previous version, it does not explain the need for the current review when similar systematic reviews exist, including identifying and citing the previous review in the rationale for this PRISMA item.
The retrieved evidence does not briefly describe a proposed mechanism of action of the interventions as part of the rationale.
The retrieved evidence does not consider or present a logic model for complex interventions/delivery contexts showing hypothesised relationships between components and outcomes.
No explicit review objective(s) or question(s) are stated in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Randomisedtrials in which people at risk of covid-19 were allocated to prophylaxis or no prophylaxis (standard care or placebo).
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence describes the intervention vs comparator as prophylaxis versus no prophylaxis, but does not explicitly state the full planned comparisons using a PICO (or variant) framework for the review objectives.

elements.quote: Weincluded randomised trials of people at risk of covid-19 that compared drugs, therapeutic doses of vitamins, or antibodies for prophylaxis against one another or against no prophylaxis (placebo or standard care, as defined by the researchers), with no restriction onlanguageofpublication. We included studies addressing people pre- or post-exposure to covid-19 and at low risk (e.g. unexposed community member) or high risk (e.g. member of the same household with one or more positive cases, contact of index case, healthcare worker or long term care resident) for covid-19.
elements.reason: Specifies eligible study design (randomised trials) and participant/exposure characteristics (pre-/post-exposure; low- vs high-risk) and an eligibility comparison (prophylaxis vs no prophylaxis or vs other prophylaxis). However, it does not specify study settings or follow-up requirements, and does not clearly cover all study-characteristic components (e.g., question-framework elements and follow-up) as required.

elements.quote: All trials were published in English. Almost all trials were registered (31, 97%) and evaluated prophylactic drugs against standard care or placebo (30, 94%). Of the 32 eligible randomised trials, 22 (69%) were published in peer reviewed journals and 10 (31%) only as preprint.
elements.reason: Report characteristics are partially specified: language (English) and publication/dissemination status (peer-reviewed vs preprint) are provided. However, dissemination year and publication/report status beyond these categories (e.g., an explicit year range) are not reported in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Fig 1 | Study selection
elements.reason: The figure is referenced, and visible evidence indicates exclusion categories including "Not a randomised trial" and "Randomised trial with no results" (among others). But the retrieved evidence does not clearly distinguish exclusion because outcomes were not measured versus exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: Among the 27 randomised trials that reported covid-19 exposure status of participants, 18 evaluated prophylactic drugs in participants without documented exposure to covid-19 (pre-exposure) and seven evaluated prophylactic drugs in participants with documented exposure to covid-19 (post-exposure). Two randomised trials evaluated prophylactic drugs in both participants pre-exposure and post-exposure to covid-19.
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence identifies groups used to classify study participants for analyses (pre-exposure vs post-exposure). However, it does not specify the groups used in each synthesis or explicitly link these groups to the comparisons defined in the review objectives.
The retrieved evidence lists exclusions (e.g., exclusions in text_13 and reasons in the study selection figure), but it does not provide rationales for any notable restrictions on study eligibility.

elements.quote: We rated trials at high risk of bias overall if one or more domains were rated as probably high risk of bias or as high risk of bias and as low risk of bias if all domains were rated as probably low risk of bias or low risk of bias.

elements.reason: Identifies syntheses that were impossible/inappropriate (precluding meta-analysis and failing network meta-analysis sample size criteria) and provides reasons.

elements.quote: We plan to perform networkmeta-regression to explore if duration of prophylactic drug use may modify the relative effect of the drug on adverse effects leading to discontinuation hypothesising that, if the drug is active at the time of exposure, it will have a greater relative effect.

elements.quote: Pending data from quantitative studies of patient values, we chose thresholds of small but important effects of 0.1% for mortality; 2% for adverse events leading to discontinuation and laboratory confirmed infection; 3% for suspected, probable, or laboratory confirmed infection; and 1% for admission to hospital.
elements.reason: Review-specific thresholds for rating certainty (small but important effects) and related rationales are reported.

elements.quote: Judgments of imprecision for this systematic review were made using a minimally contextualised approach.

elements.quote: Two methodologists with experience in using GRADE rated each domain for each comparison and outcome separately and resolved discrepancies by discussion.

elements.quote:
Conclusions Withregardtothelimitations of this review, one cluster randomised trial did not report the design effect or the intracluster correlation coefficient itself necessary to calculate the design effect, precluding adjustment in analyses-potentially leading to falsely narrow credible intervals. 33 Cluster sizes were, however, small, making substantial bias unlikely.

The living nature of our systematic review and network meta-analysis could amplify publication bias, because studies with promising results are more likely to be published and are published sooner than studies with negative results.
elements.reason: The discussion section explicitly identifies limitations related to the review process (e.g., missing design effect reporting preventing adjustment) and a limitation affecting the review (living nature potentially amplifying publication bias).
